newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Champagne to add sparkle to milestone EU meeting.
newsitem.headline: Champagne to add sparkle to milestone EU meeting.

text.p: Champagne corks are set to pop in Luxembourg on Monday, injecting fizz into laborious farm price and olive oil subsidy talks at the European Union's 2,000th ministerial meeting.

Farm ministers, famous for marathon negotiating sessions, will for once break early for some light relief although officials were anxious to calm taxpayers concerned about extravagance in the run-up to a single EU currency.

"Although the figure is worthy of a major celebration, the council -- in keeping with its tradition of austerity -- is a normal working meeting on various agricultural subjects," the EU Council secretariat said in a news release.
A Dutch EU Presidency official added that any budget overspill would be mopped up by The Hague.
The European coal and steel, economic and atomic energy communities were combined into a single ministerial council under the Treaty of Union in July 1967.

The EU Council of Ministers wears many different caps -- ranging from foreign, finance and farm to consumer and cultural affairs -- and meets about ninety times a year, mostly in Brussels, but in Luxembourg during April, June and October.
It has grown to 15 countries working in 11 languages, from six countries with four languages in 1967 and is reviewing changes to cope with eastwards expansion to 25 members.
